science.title: Green fluorescent protein and its fusion constructs induce intracellular puncta under defined conditions
science.description: Cells compartmentalize biomolecules using both membrane‑bound organelles and membrane‑less biomolecular condensates, the latter of which can be formed via liquid–liquid phase separation. Such condensates are linked to various physiological processes and disease progression; however, the evaluation of intracellular condensate formation remains challenging. Here, we examined the intracellular dynamics of three condensate-associated proteins, α-synuclein (αS), tau, and FUS, using fluorescent protein fusion constructs. Enhanced green fluorescent protein (EGFP)-fused αS and tau formed intracellular puncta upon serum removal, possibly due to elevated local protein concentrations. These puncta were sensitive to changes in cellular pH, divalent cation chelation, and the availability of metabolic substrates, and rapidly disappeared following exposure of cells to phosphate‑buffered saline. For tau–EGFP, tau-mediated microtubule binding competed with puncta formation. FUS–EGFP puncta were formed even under serum-containing conditions, exhibiting physicochemical properties distinct from those of αS–EGFP and tau–EGFP puncta. Thus, EGFP‑fused αS, tau, and FUS all formed puncta in cells. However, intracellular puncta were also observed in cells expressing EGFP without a fusion partner upon serum removal. These EGFP puncta exhibited properties similar to those of αS–EGFP and tau–EGFP puncta. Notably, the red fluorescent protein mRuby2 did not form puncta like EGFP, and serum removal failed to induce puncta formation by mRuby2‑fused αS and tau. Overall, our findings suggest that EGFP exhibits an intrinsic environment‑dependent propensity to form intracellular puncta, highlighting the importance of fluorescent protein choice and providing a basis for the reliable evaluation of condensate formation in living cells.

science.title: An evidence-based mixed-methods randomized controlled trial of a WeChat sexual health intervention for older chinese women
science.description: This mixed-methods randomized controlled trial evaluated a culturally adapted WeChat sexual health interventionfor older Chinese women. A total of 205 women aged ≥60 years were randomized to a 21-day sexual healthintervention or healthy-aging control, with assessments at baseline, post-intervention, and 2-month follow-up.Sexual function was assessed using the Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI), quality of life using the WHOQOL-OLD,and qualitative interviews were conducted with 36 participants. No signifi cant between-group diff erences were foundin FSFI scores. In contrast, WHOQOL-OLD scores were signifi cantly higher in the intervention group at post-intervention and remained modestly higher at follow-up. Qualitative fi ndings indicated improvements in emotional comfort, .relational intimacy, self-acceptance, and confi dence in discussing sexual health. The fi ndings suggest thatculturally adapted digital sexual health interventions may enhance broader quality of life among older Chinesewomen even when measurable sexual function remains unchanged, supporting greater attention to relational andpsychosocial dimensions of later-life sexual health.

science.title: From the start, the solar system chose fire over ice to build its first bodies
science.description:
When the solar system first took up the task of building solid bodies — such as planets, moons, and protoplanets — it basically had a choice between two ingredients. There were heat-forged chondrules, which were millimeter-sized bits of rock; and there was matrix, a fine-grained, cold dust loaded with water ice and organic molecules.
And from the get-go, the solar system chose fire.
In a new, Yale-led study, researchers provide the first geochemical evidence that within the first million years after the solar system began to form, it was already preferentially sorting for chondrules over matrix. Prior research had only been able to document this sorting process in objects that formed 2 to 4 million years after the solar system’s origin.
The study was published Sept. 18 in the journal Nature Astronomy.
